name: Isosorbide mononitrate
mechanism: NO donor causing venodilation and reduced preload
dosing: Dosing depends on formulation (immediate- or modified-release); commonly 20–60 mg daily for chronic angina—follow product-specific guidance and allow a nitrate-free interval to reduce tolerance
contraindications: Concurrent phosphodiesterase-5 (PDE5) inhibitor use, marked hypotension, severe anaemia, increased intracranial pressure, known hypersensitivity
interactions: Co-administration with PDE5 inhibitors can cause profound hypotension; additive hypotensive effects with other vasodilators or antihypertensives
monitoring: Monitor blood pressure, heart rate and symptomatic response; check for development of postural symptoms and headaches
pregnancy: Use only if clinically essential with specialist advice
sideEffects: Common: headache, flushing, hypotension; reflex tachycardia; long-term use requires nitrate-free interval to prevent tolerance
clinicalPearls: Isosorbide mononitrate preferred for once-daily chronic prophylaxis due to longer duration; ensure daily nitrate-free period to reduce tolerance; educate patients about timing
indication: Prevention of angina (chronic stable angina) and symptomatic relief in selected patients with heart failure
